 SECTIONS Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s 10-year-old daughter vibe-codes several creations, including a messaging app, apps similar to GeoCities and a game inspired by FarmVille, with each project also featuring its own marketing and sales plan By Trending Desk , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 08, 2026, 03:43:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Maxima Zuckerberg, daughter of Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, is interested in artificial intelligence and software development. She is currently experimenting with vibe-coding, which uses natural language to create software with AI tools. While her parents support her enthusiasm, they have imposed restrictions on developing online projects. Priscilla Chan specifically did not allow Maxima to create a dating website due to safety concerns.
 Agencies Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s 10-year-old daughter vibe-codes several creations, including a messaging app, apps similar to GeoCities and a game inspired by FarmVille, with each project also featuring its own marketing and sales plan Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s 10-year-old daughter, Maxima, is developing an early interest in artificial intelligence and software development. The couple’s eldest daughter has started experimenting with “vibe-coding”, a method of creating software and digital applications with the help of AI tools and natural language instructions.
 However, while her parents encourage her to explore technology and turn her ideas into reality, there are certain limits to what she can create. Priscilla Chan recently revealed that she does not allow Maxima to develop projects that are accessible to the internet. The restriction has even prevented the youngster from pursuing an unusual idea: building a dating website.
In an interview with Colossus, Chan spoke about her daughter's growing interest in technology and the rules she has established around her experiments. 
“She’s quite limited, because Mom doesn’t let her build things that are open to the internet. Like, she wanted to build a dating site. That was a no,” Chan said.
 Maxima Has A Natural Interest In Building Things, Says Priscilla Chan
Chan also spoke about how her daughter's enthusiasm for creating things developed naturally, without her parents having to introduce or encourage the interest.
 Live Events
 “She just has a desire to build things that is innate, that we didn’t teach her. It just came. She’s delighted by the idea of bringing something into the world,” she said.
 Maxima's interest appears to extend beyond simply using technology. Through coding experiments, she is exploring how ideas can be transformed into functional digital projects.
 However, Chan's restrictions mean that these creations must remain within certain boundaries, particularly when it comes to making them available online. Chan walked through some of her daughter's vibe-coded creations, like a messaging app. There were also apps similar to GeoCities and the game FarmVille, according to Colossus. Like her father, Zuckerberg's daughter seems to have an entrepreneurial spirit. Each app included a plan for marketing and sales plan.
 What Is Vibe-Coding? How AI Is Helping Children Build Software
Vibe-coding refers to a method of software development in which users describe what they want to create using everyday language, and AI tools generate the corresponding code.
Rather than manually writing programming instructions, users can provide prompts, review the results and ask the AI to make changes until the project matches their requirements.
The approach has gained attention as generative AI tools make software development more accessible to people without extensive coding experience.
For young learners, vibe-coding can offer an opportunity to experiment with application development, games and other digital projects. However, AI-generated code still needs to be checked, particularly when applications involve internet access, personal information or interactions with other users.
 Mark Zuckerberg Has Introduced His Children To Scratch, Robotics And 3D Printing
Maxima's interest in coding is not a recent development in the Zuckerberg household. Mark Zuckerberg has previously discussed introducing his daughters to programming through Scratch, a visual coding platform designed to help children create games, animations and interactive stories.
The children have also explored other tools and activities, including Replit, Google Docs, Kano, robotics and 3D printing.
Zuckerberg has shared his interest in building robots alongside his daughters, with the family experimenting with different designs and hardware.
Their projects have reportedly involved Raspberry Pi and Nvidia Jetson devices to run language models, allowing the children to explore the connection between physical computing and artificial intelligence.
These activities form part of the family's efforts to introduce the children to different aspects of technology through practical, hands-on experiences.
 Zuckerberg’s Daughter August Has Used Meta AI To Create A Book
Maxima's younger sister, August, has also been exploring technology through coding and creative projects.
She reportedly works on Minecraft and Scratch projects and has also created a book titled The Mermaid Crystal.
For the project, August used Meta AI to help generate illustrations and create a trailer, combining storytelling with generative artificial intelligence.
Her experience demonstrates how AI tools can be used for creative activities beyond software development, including writing, visual storytelling and digital content creation.
